study type: Retrospective cohort study with cross-sectional analysis
cohort: The study included 6506 women of reproductive age (average 28.7 years) who had undergone HPV testing and genotyping at gynecological departments in Ningbo, China, between 2016 and 2020.
finding: Persistent high-risk HPV infection was significantly associated with a higher risk of reproductive tract inflammation, miscarriage, reduced live birth rate, and increased cesarean section rate among women of reproductive age.
mod_finding: HPV infection was associated with a higher cesarean section rate.
cross-section timing: During pregnancy, within the study period of 2016-2020
